posts.title: Fossil Footprint Nebula
posts.description: The Fossil Footprint Nebula This is the Fossil Footprint Nebula, NGC 1491, about 10,700 light-years away in Perseus. The bright blue-green center is surrounded by a much larger cloud of glowing gas. I captured it over October 21 and 22 with my EdgeHD 11 and OGMA AP26MC, using ten-minute exposures through sulfur, hydrogen and oxygen filters. posts.title: Rose Galaxies
posts.description: A rose for Hubble’s 21st anniversary For Hubble’s 21st anniversary in 2011, astronomers released a portrait of these two interacting galaxies, Arp 273, commonly called the Rose Galaxies. It’s easy to see why they picked them. The larger galaxy’s arms curl around its center like petals, with the smaller galaxy stretched out beside it. posts.title: Teaching astrophotography, with a little help from AI
posts.description: As part of my commitment to disclose AI authorship , this article was partially authored with AI. I’ve built an interactive guide to astrophotography calibration and stacking , using photographs from my backyard observatory.
